prompts.5:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production pixel-art game sprite parts sheet, ONE level-5 upgrade of the existing Sharpshooter precision trebuchet tower.
Reference 1: ORIGINAL three stone-topped rectangular wood towers. Reference 2: enlarged ORIGINAL weapon; it is a narrow vertical wooden throwing LEVER with a chunky square steel counterweight at the TOP, an axle at its center, a spoon/pouch holding a bright yellow-green gemstone shot at the BOTTOM. It is NOT a gun, bow or slingshot. Preserve this unmistakable identity.
Three entirely separate components in ONE HORIZONTAL ROW, transparent background, wide empty gaps. LEFT: stationary compact rectangular tower base, shallow grey stone parapet around empty flat grey top platform, warm reddish wood plank facade and grey footing, tiny green inlay. No weapon on this base. MIDDLE: detached single lever weapon, counterweight at TOP, spoon at BOTTOM, ready pose pointing vertically UP. Narrow reinforced redwood arm, silver iron end caps, visible central axle, one loaded yellow-green gem in bottom spoon. RIGHT: matching single faceted yellow-green projectile with white highlight, no aura/trail.
This is LEVEL 5: practical modest iron reinforcements, grey stone, reddish wood. Strong simple pixel clusters, limited palette, crisp dark contour, no blur/gradients/rendered surfaces. Straight-on slightly elevated game view, symmetrical front, see top and front facade, NEVER diagonal/isometric view.
Readability at base64x84 pixels and lever32x62 pixels. Keep parapet LOW, flat top, short front wall, no extra turrets or columns, no growth in footprint/height. Same family as supplied original. No labels/text, no background, no shadows, no grid. Large visible spacing between all three components; no tiny decorative flecks outside sprites.
